newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Squeezing in again to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Squeezing in again to U.S..

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads tightened against the U.S., albeit trading above the day's lows late in the day, as the local market braced itself for this week's key data for inflation and wages.

Analysts expect spreads could tighten further if as expected the inflation report proves extremely benign, and could see the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread test resistance at 25 basis points.

"In addition to the excellent inflation fundamentals released this week, the international environment may see Australian bond increasing attractive," said Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale.
Maguire pointed to today's French Public Audit which may again highlight the likely softness of the Euro and undermine the core European markets.
"In this environment, U.S. Treasuries, U.K. Gilts and possibly Australian bonds are likely to benefit," he added.

U.S. Treasuries weakened on Friday as the market showed jitters ahead of this week's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan. There was no trading in U.S. debt in Asia due to a Japanese holiday.

Meanwhile, New Zealand debt staged a minor rebound with the New Zealand dollar after last Friday's huge sell-off, although any sign of renewed weakness in the currency will quickly put the market back on defensive again.
